correctness.rationale: The exact six annihilator classes and their complete adjacency are published for a product of three fields. For fields of equal order at least three, each class contains at least two false twins, forcing at most one initially white vertex per class; with one or zero white vertices per class the process is exactly a six-label unique-neighbor peeling process. All label subsets are checked symbolically: every subset through size three peels, twelve of fifteen four-subsets peel, and none larger does. This yields the complete weighted polynomial. A rank-four quotient adjacency matrix gives a real graph-pattern witness and the standard maximum-nullity bound makes it optimal. The binary-field boundary is handled separately by an exact triangular-prism count and rank-three Gram witness.

value.rationale: The theorem determines every coefficient of the zero forcing polynomial for a natural infinite family of reduced annihilator graphs and classifies all minimum forcing sets. It also exhibits a stable inverse-eigenvalue phenomenon: for all field orders at least three, real minimum rank is exactly four while graph order grows quadratically. The weighted twelve-profile description explains the parameter structurally and is not a routine restatement of the known clique/chromatic decomposition.
